title: Live Visibility
eyebrow: Proposal · thread links that always show, and long work that never goes quiet

short.lead: You asked for two things now, not after the restructure (#306, reverted on 2026-10-28): every thread shows its own session link without being asked, and long work never looks stuck. I found why the link is missing: the plugin only builds it when CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECTS_SESSION is 1. This very session is a cloud session started with CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 and a valid cse_ id, but CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECTS_SESSION is unset here, so no link was offered. Even inside a project thread, the link only appears in a checklist header, so a thread that never posts a checklist never shows it.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what exists today and what this proposal adds.
items: Builds https://claude.ai/code/session_<id> from CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID. It is reused as it is; only the gate in front of it and where the link must appear change.
Blocks the end of a turn once when a Remote Control link or helper work trail was never posted. It gains one more case: the session's own link missing from the first reply.

Reads how long ago a helper's transcript or a command's output file was last written, and prints ok, STALLED or finished. Nothing calls it any more: #292 removed the 5-minute reminder on 2026-10-15. This proposal reuses it as the source of each progress line.

Dropped in #292 together with a guard that refused nohup, & and hidden windows. The guard stays dropped. Choice 4 ("Does a \"never hide\" rule come back?") asks whether a short rule in your wording comes back.

When nothing you can see has been posted for 2 minutes, the thread posts one line: what it is doing, how long it has run, and when the work last wrote anything (from stallcheck). A STALLED line says so in words and names what the work is blocked on.

I read it as a long helper agent or a long command, where today you see only the start and the end. If Trace is the name of a specific tool or step, tell me its name, because a hook can be pinned to it directly.
If my reading is wrong, put the name of the tool or step in your reply.

changes: chg
Changed gate: every cloud session with a session id gets its link (thread_link_note)
The link is offered whenever CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is true and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID has the cse_ shape, not only in project threads.
A cloud session started from a project thread, like this one, gets no link and is hard to find again.
Its first reply opens with "Transcript of this session" as a link, with the raw id beside it.
Checked on this session's own variables: CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true, a cse_ id, CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECTS_SESSION unset. Links still never reach git, because the credit guard from #405 is unchanged.
chg
Changed rule text: the link opens the first reply, plus the checklist header in a project thread
The injected instruction asks for the link at the top of the first reply, and the links-owed check blocks once if it is missing.
The link appears only if a checklist is posted.
The link is the first thing you see in every thread.
In a plain cloud session there is no post_message tool, so the check reads the first reply's text instead.
chg
New hook: progress lines (PostToolUse, every tool, project threads and cloud sessions)
Keeps one timestamp file per session. After 2 minutes without a visible post, the next tool result tells the thread to post a progress line first.
The thread can run for many minutes with nothing posted.
You get a line at least every 2 minutes while the thread is making tool calls.

Cost: one small file read per tool call, no network. A hook fires only between tool calls, so a single call that runs for 10 minutes still goes quiet. The next row, on background helpers and commands, covers that gap.
chg
Changed instruction: long helpers and commands run in the background with a watch

A helper or command expected to run over 1 minute starts in the background, and the thread starts stallcheck.py --watch --every 120 under Monitor. Each line it prints wakes the thread, which posts it.
A foreground helper blocks the thread for its whole run, so nothing can be posted.
Each line reads, for example: "builder: still working, last wrote 14 s ago" or "builder: STALLED, nothing written for 6 min".

UNTESTED: I have not yet confirmed that a Monitor line wakes a project thread; the build proves it on a real thread before anything relies on it. stallcheck gains one flag, --every, to print a status line at a fixed interval, here every 120 seconds.
chg
Rule text: nothing is hidden without an easy way to see it

One section in house-rules.md, in your words: work, thoughts and processes are never hidden in a way you can't easily find; anything quieted (such as HOUSE_RULES_TRACE lines) names the switch that shows it.
Since #292 there is no rule about this at all.
Wherever something is quiet by default, it says how to turn it up.
Only if you pick option A under "Does a \"never hide\" rule come back?"
choices: sessions
Which sessions show their own link?
A
Every cloud session with a session id, including sessions a project thread starts
Covers the case you hit: this session had no link.
B
Project threads only, as today
Smallest change, but cloud sessions stay linkless.
Option A fixes the session you are reading now.
where
Where does the link appear?
A
First line of the first reply, plus the checklist header in a project thread, enforced by the end-of-turn check
You see it without opening anything.
B
Checklist header only, as today
Threads without a checklist never show it.
Option A makes it show by default, which is what you asked for.
quiet
How is long work kept visible?
A
Progress lines every 2 minutes, and long helpers and commands run in the background under a stallcheck watch
Closes both gaps: quiet between tool calls, and quiet inside one long call.
B
Progress lines only
Simpler, but a single long helper still goes quiet for its whole run.
C
Option A, plus the helper's work trail file rewritten at each progress line
You can read the helper's commands mid-run, at the cost of one file write every 2 minutes.
Option A answers "is it stuck?" with a line that says so.
rule
Does a "never hide" rule come back?
A
Yes: one short section, in your wording, with no guard refusing commands
Puts your standard in writing so every session reads it.
B
No rule text: the hooks above are enough
Less rule text loaded each session.
Option A, because the hooks only cover the cases I thought of.

wrapup.summary: Every cloud session and project thread opens with its own transcript link, and long work posts a progress line at least every 2 minutes, saying STALLED in words when it is stuck.
wrapup.changing: One gate and one instruction in house_rules/delegation.py, one new progress hook, one new stallcheck.py flag, an optional rule section, plus tests, docs and a version bump. It builds on today's 2.74.1 code, not the reverted restructure.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the four choices above, and whether my reading of "running a Trace" is right.
wrapup.next: I file the build issues, build on AjsAgent/thread-links-trace-visibility-4eoxf3, prove the progress line on a real project thread, and hand it over with a QA page.
